headline: A web fetcher feeds an extractor and downstream summarizer — prompt injection from fetched pages is the headline risk.
name: Browser → Extract → Summarize

conditions: extracted content includes unsanitized HTML or JavaScript
mitigations: extract only text content, not scripts
mark extracted content as untrusted in summarizer prompt
A_prompt_injection.rationale: Raw HTML from arbitrary web pages contains scripts, forms, and user-controlled content. Extractor parses this without sanitization, allowing injected prompts to influence downstream summarization.

conditions: fetched pages contain auth tokens or PII in URLs or HTML
B_data_leakage.rationale: Fetched pages may contain embedded user data, cookies, or authentication tokens in URL parameters. Extractor writes raw HTML to disk, exposing this to multiple downstream tools.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Extractor and summarizer are both writers but operate sequentially on different data streams (HTML vs extracted text), limiting conflict.

mitigations: verify page load completion before extract
D_cascading_error.rationale: If browser fetch returns partial or corrupted HTML, extractor may miss content that summarizer then cannot recover from; no validation of fetch completeness.

E_compliance.rationale: Fetching arbitrary web pages generally does not involve regulated data unless the target site itself serves compliance-sensitive content.
